title: Build a fixed-size circular buffer in Go
description: Greenfield Go task: implement a ring buffer (circular buffer) with fixed capacity, supporting Push, Pop, Peek, Len, Cap, IsEmpty, and IsFull.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement RingBuf in internal/ring/ring.go.

package ring

import "errors"

type RingBuf struct {
    buf  []int
    head int  // index of the next item to Pop
    tail int  // index of the next empty slot to Push into
    len  int
    cap  int
}

func New(cap int) *RingBuf
func (r *RingBuf) Push(v int) error   // returns error if full
func (r *RingBuf) Pop() (int, error)  // returns (value, nil) or (0, error) if empty
func (r *RingBuf) Peek() (int, error) // peek at head without consuming; error if empty
func (r *RingBuf) Len() int
func (r *RingBuf) Cap() int
func (r *RingBuf) IsEmpty() bool
func (r *RingBuf) IsFull() bool

Wrap head and tail indices using modulo (% cap).
All 6 tests in internal/ring/ring_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: RingBuf stores items in a circular array with head and tail pointers
Wrap-around works correctly after pop+push at capacity
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
